title: Dynamics 365 Business Central: design custom AI agents with the AI development toolkit
summary: Hold: the instructions for reaching agent permissions and profiles omit the wizard's required choice between creating an agent from scratch and using a template. The roadmap facts, preview restrictions and documented billing model are supported. The capacity-allocation API exists, but its presentation and the governance checklist need minor corrections.

claims.claim: Power Platform admin center > Licensing > Products > Copilot Studio > Summary > Prepaid capacity > Manage Capacity leads to credit allocation.
claims.quote: Select Manage Capacity from the Prepaid capacity card. ... In the allocation panel, select an environment and specify the number of Copilot Credits to allocate in the Copilot Credits textbox.
claims.fix: Complete the path as 'Licensing > Products > Copilot Studio > Summary > Prepaid capacity > Manage Capacity > environment > Copilot Credits'. The printed navigation is correct; it omits only environment selection and the allocation field.

claims.claim: PUT licensing/allocationsV2 with api-version=2024-10-01 writes an environment allocation using the printed scope and MCSMessages quantity properties.
claims.quote: scope = @{ environmentId = $environmentId } ... entitlementId = "MCSMessages" ... allocation = @{ quantity = 5000 } ... Invoke-RestMethod -Method Put ... "$apiBaseUrl/licensing/allocationsV2?api-version=$apiVersion"
claims.fix: Replace the call with 'PUT https://api.powerplatform.com/licensing/allocationsV2?api-version=2024-10-01'. Add to the note: 'The request body identifies scope.environmentId and sets allocatedEntitlements[].entitlementId to MCSMessages and allocatedEntitlements[].allocation.quantity to the credit allocation.' The printed body keys are correct, but the standard puts them in the note, not the call.

claims.where: Governance controls: Create agent wizard permissions path
claims.claim: The printed Agent > Create route proceeds directly to Permissions > Manage permissions without a wizard branch choice.
claims.quote: In the Create agent wizard, choose whether to create a blank agent or use a template. ... To create a blank agent, choose Create agent from scratch ... Under Permissions, use Manage permissions
claims.fix: Replace the wizard-navigation sentence with: 'To configure a blank agent, select Agent > Create > Create agent from scratch. After entering its identity details, use Setup profile under Profile (role), and Manage permissions under Permissions.' This includes the required wizard choice documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/dynamics365/business-central/dev-itpro/ai/ai-development-toolkit-agent-create.

claims.where: Governance controls: Create agent wizard profile path
claims.claim: The printed Agent > Create route proceeds directly to Profile (role) > Setup profile without a wizard branch choice.
claims.quote: In the Create agent wizard, choose whether to create a blank agent or use a template. ... To create a blank agent, choose Create agent from scratch ... Under Profile (role), use the Setup profile option
claims.fix: Use the same replacement for the shared wizard-navigation sentence: 'To configure a blank agent, select Agent > Create > Create agent from scratch. After entering its identity details, use Setup profile under Profile (role), and Manage permissions under Permissions.' Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/dynamics365/business-central/dev-itpro/ai/ai-development-toolkit-agent-create.

claims.claim: Learn documents AL Agent.UpdateAccessControl for assigning agent permission sets.
claims.quote: The UpdateAccessControl method replaces any existing permission sets with the ones you provide: ... Agent.UpdateAccessControl(AgentUserSecurityID, TempAccessControlBuffer);

claims.claim: Learn documents AL Agent.SetProfile for assigning an agent profile.
claims.quote: // Assign a profile ... Agent.SetProfile(AgentUserSecurityID, 'ACCOUNTANT', SystemApplicationAppId);

claims.claim: The AL configuration methods are restricted across application boundaries, not unrestricted administrator APIs for designer-created agents.
claims.quote: it's only possible to use the AI development toolkit to interact with agents defined in your own application. Creating instances, tasks, messages and any configuration changes targeting an agent defined in a different application is blocked with an error.

claims.claim: The cited Assign permissions page explains how to grant permission sets to Business Central users.
claims.quote: You can assign permissions sets to users in two ways: From the User Card page, by selecting permission sets to assign to the user. From the Permission Set by User page, by selecting users that a permission set is assigned to.

claims.claim: The roadmap recommends storing exported agent definitions in source control.
